## Introduction

For this market baseline, we are using job-posting data from Computer Systems Design and Related Services industry (NAICS 5415). We look at job titles, locations, work arrangements, salaries, and analytics tools mentioned in the job descriptions. This will help us understand the opportunities shown in our data and give us a starting point for comparing them with our team’s skills.

We began by checking how much data we have and what information is available. We then looked at missing values, converted usable salary ranges into annual amounts, and created charts to make the patterns easier to understand. We found some limitations along the way, including missing location information, unknown work arrangements, and roles outside our intended analytics focus.

```{python}
        COUNT(NULLIF(TRIM(state), '')) AS with_state,
        COUNT(NULLIF(TRIM(state_code), '')) AS with_state_code
    FROM job_facts
```

```{python}
#| output: false
work_arrangements = spark.sql("""
    WITH counts AS (
        SELECT
            COALESCE(
                NULLIF(TRIM(remote_status), ''),
                'Unknown'
            ) AS work_arrangement,
            COUNT(*) AS postings
        FROM job_facts
        GROUP BY 1
    )
    SELECT
        work_arrangement,
        postings,
        ROUND(
            100.0 * postings / SUM(postings) OVER (),
            1
        ) AS percent_of_postings
    FROM counts
    ORDER BY postings DESC
""")

work_arrangements.show(truncate=False)
```

## Salary coverage and currency checks

```{python}
salary_coverage = spark.sql("""
    SELECT
        COUNT(*) AS total_postings,
        SUM(CASE
            WHEN annual_salary_min IS NOT NULL
             AND annual_salary_max IS NOT NULL
            THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END) AS with_annual_range,
        SUM(CASE
            WHEN hourly_salary_min IS NOT NULL
             AND hourly_salary_max IS NOT NULL
            THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END) AS with_hourly_range,
        SUM(CASE
            WHEN annual_salary_min IS NULL
             AND annual_salary_max IS NULL
             AND hourly_salary_min IS NULL
             AND hourly_salary_max IS NULL
            THEN 1 ELSE 0
        END) AS without_numeric_salary
    FROM job_facts
""")

salary_coverage.toPandas().T.rename(columns={0: "Value"})
```

```{python}
#| output: false
spark.sql("""
    SELECT
        title,
        location_text,
        salary_text,
        annual_salary_min,
        annual_salary_max
    FROM job_facts
    WHERE annual_salary_min IS NOT NULL
      AND annual_salary_max IS NOT NULL
    ORDER BY location_text, job_id
    LIMIT 20
""").show(20, truncate=100)
```

```{python}
#| output: false
from pyspark.sql import functions as F

has_annual = (
    F.col("annual_salary_min").isNotNull()
    & F.col("annual_salary_max").isNotNull()
)

has_hourly = (
    F.col("hourly_salary_min").isNotNull()
    & F.col("hourly_salary_max").isNotNull()
)

currency_code = F.regexp_extract(
    F.upper(F.coalesce(F.col("salary_text"), F.lit(""))),
    r"\b(USD|CAD|EUR|GBP|AUD|NZD|INR|SGD|JPY|CHF|CNY|AED)\b",
    1
)

jobs_pay = (
    jobs_clean
    .withColumn(
        "annualized_min",
        F.when(has_annual, F.col("annual_salary_min"))
         .when(has_hourly, F.col("hourly_salary_min") * 2080)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "annualized_max",
        F.when(has_annual, F.col("annual_salary_max"))
         .when(has_hourly, F.col("hourly_salary_max") * 2080)
    )
    .withColumn(
        "salary_basis",
        F.when(has_annual, "Reported annual")
         .when(has_hourly, "Hourly converted × 2080")
         .otherwise("No complete range")
    )
    .withColumn(
        "salary_currency",
        F.when(currency_code != "", currency_code)
         .otherwise("Unconfirmed")
    )
)

jobs_pay.filter(F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull()) \
    .groupBy("salary_currency", "salary_basis").count() \
    .orderBy(F.desc("count")) \
    .show(truncate=False)
```

```{python}
# Identify US locations from country labels or state abbreviations.
us_states = (
    "AL|AK|AZ|AR|CA|CO|CT|DE|FL|GA|HI|ID|IL|IN|IA|KS|KY|LA|"
    "ME|MD|MA|MI|MN|MS|MO|MT|NE|NV|NH|NJ|NM|NY|NC|ND|OH|OK|"
    "OR|PA|RI|SC|SD|TN|TX|UT|VT|VA|WA|WV|WI|WY|DC"
)

location = F.upper(F.coalesce(F.col("location_text"), F.lit("")))

us_location = (
    location.rlike(r"\bUNITED STATES\b|\bUSA\b|\bU\.S\.A?\.")
    | location.rlike(r",\s*(" + us_states + r")\b")
    | location.rlike(
        r"\b(ARIZONA|TEXAS|CALIFORNIA|FLORIDA|MARYLAND|"
        r"MICHIGAN|MISSOURI|NEW YORK)\b"
    )
    | location.rlike(r"\bLOS ANGELES METROPOLITAN AREA\b")
)

assume_usd = (
    (F.col("salary_currency") == "Unconfirmed")
    & us_location
)

jobs_pay = (
    jobs_pay
    .withColumn(
        "currency_basis",
        F.when(assume_usd, "Assumed from US location")
        .when(
            F.col("salary_currency") != "Unconfirmed",
            "Explicit currency in salary text"
        )
        .otherwise("Unconfirmed")
    )
    .withColumn(
        "salary_currency",
        F.when(assume_usd, "USD")
        .otherwise(F.col("salary_currency"))
    )
)

jobs_pay.filter(
    F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull()
).groupBy(
    "salary_currency", "currency_basis"
).count().orderBy(F.desc("count")).toPandas()
```


```{python}
#| output: false
usd_pay = (
    jobs_pay
    .filter(
        (F.col("salary_currency") == "USD")
        & F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull()
        & F.col("annualized_max").isNotNull()
    )
    .withColumn(
        "annual_midpoint",
        (F.col("annualized_min") + F.col("annualized_max")) / 2
    )
)

usd_pay.agg(
    F.count("*").alias("postings"),
    F.round(
        F.percentile_approx("annual_midpoint", 0.5), 2
    ).alias("median_annual_midpoint_usd"),
    F.round(
        F.avg("annual_midpoint"), 2
    ).alias("mean_annual_midpoint_usd")
).show(truncate=False)
```
```{python}
#| output: false
jobs_pay.filter(
    (F.col("annualized_min").isNotNull())
    & (F.col("salary_currency") == "Unconfirmed")
).select(
    "location_text",
    "salary_text",
    "salary_basis"
).orderBy(
    "location_text", "salary_text"
).show(30, truncate=100)
```

```{python}

usd_role_pay = (
    usd_pay
    .withColumn(

                F.trim(F.col("normalized_title"))
```

## Checking the structured skills data

```{python}
#| output: false
jobs_clean.filter(
    F.col("skills").isNotNull()
    & (F.trim(F.col("skills")) != "")
    & (F.trim(F.col("skills")) != "[]")
).select(
    "title",
    "skills"
).show(5, truncate=False)
```

```{python}
#| output: false
skills_parsed = jobs_clean.withColumn(
    "skills_array",
    F.from_json(
        F.col("skills"),
        "array<struct<name:string,type:string,confidence:double>>"
    )
)

# Check how many postings have usable skill information.
skills_parsed.agg(
    F.count("*").alias("total_postings"),
    F.sum(
        F.when(F.size("skills_array") > 0, 1).otherwise(0)
    ).alias("postings_with_skills")
).show(truncate=False)

# Extract skill names and count distinct postings.
job_skills = (
    skills_parsed
    .select("job_id", F.explode("skills_array").alias("skill_record"))
    .select(
        "job_id",
        F.lower(F.trim(F.col("skill_record.name"))).alias("skill")
    )
    .filter(F.col("skill").isNotNull() & (F.col("skill") != ""))
    .dropDuplicates(["job_id", "skill"])
)

skill_demand = (
    job_skills
    .groupBy("skill")
    .agg(F.countDistinct("job_id").alias("postings"))
    .orderBy(F.desc("postings"), "skill")
)

skill_demand.show(20, truncate=False)
```

```{python}
#| output: false

skills_parsed.groupBy(
    F.size("skills_array").alias("skills_per_posting")
).count().orderBy("skills_per_posting").show(30, truncate=False)

# Look for common analytics tools anywhere in the recorded skills.
skill_demand.filter(
    F.col("skill").rlike(
        r"sql|python|tableau|power\s*bi|excel|"
        r"pandas|spark|statistics|visualization"

).show(50, truncate=False)
```

```{python}
has_description = (
    F.col("description").isNotNull()
    & (F.length(F.trim(F.col("description"))) > 0)
)

jobs_clean.agg(
```

```{python}
#| output: false
tool_patterns = [
    ("SQL", r"\bsql\b"),
    ("Python", r"\bpython\b"),
  ("Excel", r"\bexcel\b(?!\s+(?:in|at|as|within)\b)"),
    ("Tableau", r"\btableau\b"),
    ("Power BI", r"\bpower[\s-]*bi\b"),
    ("Apache Spark / PySpark", r"\b(?:apache\s+spark|pyspark)\b"),
    ("Pandas", r"\bpandas\b")
]

description_jobs = jobs_clean.filter(has_description).withColumn(
    "description_lower",
    F.lower(F.col("description"))
)

description_count = description_jobs.select("job_id").distinct().count()

tool_mentions = (
    description_jobs
    .select(
        "job_id",
        F.explode(F.array(*[
            F.struct(
                F.lit(tool).alias("tool"),
                F.col("description_lower").rlike(pattern).alias("mentioned")
            )
            for tool, pattern in tool_patterns
        ])).alias("match")
    )
    .groupBy(F.col("match.tool").alias("tool"))
    .agg(
        F.countDistinct(
            F.when(F.col("match.mentioned"), F.col("job_id"))
        ).alias("postings_mentioning_tool")
    )
    .withColumn(
        "percent_of_descriptions",
        F.round(
            F.col("postings_mentioning_tool") / description_count * 100, 1
        )
    )
    .orderBy(F.desc("postings_mentioning_tool"), "tool")
)

tool_mentions.show(truncate=False)
```

```{python}
        r"(?s)(.{0,80}\bexcel\b.{0,80})",
        1
    ).alias("excel_context")
).show(10, truncate=False)
```

## Tools mentioned in job descriptions

```{python}
import plotly.express as px

tool_chart_data = tool_mentions.toPandas().sort_values(
    "postings_mentioning_tool",
    ascending=False
)

fig_tools = px.bar(
    tool_chart_data,
    x="postings_mentioning_tool",
    y="tool",
    orientation="h",
    text="postings_mentioning_tool",
    hover_data={"percent_of_descriptions": ":.1f"},
    labels={
        "postings_mentioning_tool": "Postings mentioning tool",
        "tool": "Tool",
        "percent_of_descriptions": "Descriptions (%)"
    },
    title="Selected Analytics Tools Mentioned in Job Descriptions",
    template="plotly_white"
)

fig_tools.update_yaxes(
    categoryorder="array",
    categoryarray=tool_chart_data["tool"].tolist(),
    autorange="reversed"
)

fig_tools.update_traces(
    marker_color="#2563EB",
    textposition="outside",
    cliponaxis=False
)

fig_tools.update_layout(
    height=450,
    margin=dict(l=30, r=70, t=80, b=50),
    xaxis=dict(
        range=[0, tool_chart_data["postings_mentioning_tool"].max() * 1.15]
    )
)

fig_tools.show()
```

SQL and Python were the most frequently mentioned tools among the seven we checked, appearing in 38.3% and 35.8% of job descriptions. This gives us a starting point for comparing employer mentions with our team’s skills. We used descriptions because the structured skills field appeared incomplete. A mention does not always mean the tool is required.

## Work arrangements

```{python}
work_chart_data = (
    jobs_clean
    .groupBy("remote_status")
    .count()
    .toPandas()
    .sort_values("count", ascending=False)
)

work_chart_data["percent"] = (
    work_chart_data["count"] / work_chart_data["count"].sum() * 100
).round(1)

fig_work = px.bar(
    work_chart_data,
    x="remote_status",
    y="count",
    text="count",
    color="remote_status",
    color_discrete_map={
        "Unknown": "#9CA3AF",
        "Hybrid": "#2563EB",
        "Remote": "#059669",
        "On-site": "#D97706"
    },
    hover_data={"percent": ":.1f"},
    labels={
        "remote_status": "Work arrangement",
        "count": "Postings",
        "percent": "Postings (%)"
    },
    title="Recorded Work Arrangements",
    template="plotly_white"
)

fig_work.update_traces(textposition="outside", cliponaxis=False)
fig_work.update_layout(
    showlegend=False,
    height=420,
    yaxis=dict(range=[0, work_chart_data["count"].max() * 1.15])
)

fig_work.show()
```

Hybrid and remote postings were almost equal, with 518 hybrid and 510 remote roles, compared with 254 on-site roles. However, 1,071 postings, or 45.5%, had an unknown work arrangement. This limits how much we can conclude about work arrangements across the full sample.

## Most common job titles

```{python}
role_chart_data = (
    jobs_clean
    .withColumn(
        "role",
        F.coalesce(
            F.when(
                F.trim(F.col("normalized_title")) != "",
                F.trim(F.col("normalized_title"))
            ),
            F.trim(F.col("title"))
        )
    )
    .filter(F.col("role").isNotNull() & (F.col("role") != ""))
    .groupBy("role")
    .agg(F.countDistinct("job_id").alias("postings"))
    .orderBy(F.desc("postings"), "role")
    .limit(15)
    .toPandas()
)

fig_roles = px.bar(
    role_chart_data,
    x="postings",
    y="role",
    orientation="h",
    text="postings",
    labels={"postings": "Postings", "role": "Recorded job title"},
    title="Top 15 Recorded Job Titles",
    template="plotly_white"
)

fig_roles.update_yaxes(
    categoryorder="array",
    categoryarray=role_chart_data["role"].tolist(),
    autorange="reversed"
)

fig_roles.update_traces(
    marker_color="#2563EB",
    textposition="outside",
    cliponaxis=False
)

fig_roles.update_layout(
    height=650,
    margin=dict(l=30, r=60, t=80, b=50),
    xaxis=dict(range=[0, role_chart_data["postings"].max() * 1.15])
)

fig_roles.show()
```

This graph shows the most common recorded job titles in our current sample. We also found attorney and HR titles outside our intended analytics focus, which showed that the initial filter needs further review. The chart helps us understand what was collected, but we need a more focused sample before drawing conclusions about analytics opportunities.

## Annualized salary distribution

```{python}
salary_chart_data = usd_pay.select("annual_midpoint").toPandas()
salary_median = salary_chart_data["annual_midpoint"].median()

fig_salary = px.histogram(
    salary_chart_data,
    x="annual_midpoint",
    nbins=30,
    labels={"annual_midpoint": "Annualized salary midpoint (USD)"},
    title=f"Annualized Salary Midpoints ({len(salary_chart_data):,} Postings)",
    template="plotly_white"
)

fig_salary.update_traces(marker_color="#2563EB")

fig_salary.add_vline(
    x=salary_median,
    line_dash="dash",
    line_color="#D97706",
    annotation_text=f"Median: ${salary_median:,.0f}",
    annotation_position="top right"
)

fig_salary.update_layout(
    height=450,
    xaxis_tickprefix="$",
    xaxis_tickformat=",",
    yaxis_title="Number of postings",
    bargap=0.05
)

fig_salary.show()
```

For the 441 postings included in this salary analysis, the median annualized salary midpoint was $134,250. The distribution has a tail toward higher salaries, showing that some advertised ranges were much higher than others. These are advertised range midpoints rather than actual earnings, and the sample combines different roles and experience levels. Hourly salaries were converted using 2,080 hours per year, and some currencies were assumed to be USD.
